name: How long does a bathtub replacement usually take?

mainEntity.name: How long does a bathtub replacement usually take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard bathtub replacement typically takes two to five days to complete, depending on the scope of the project. A straightforward swap involving an identical footprint and existing plumbing connections moves the fastest. The timeline extends if the project requires moving rough-in plumbing lines, replacing water-damaged subflooring, repairing surrounding drywall, or installing custom tile surrounds. Once the tub and surround are set, materials such as tile grout, silicone caulking, and mortar need at least 24 hours to cure before you can use the shower or bath.
acceptedAnswer.description: A standard bathtub replacement generally takes two to five days. Custom tile work, drywall repairs, plumbing adjustments, and curing times can extend the timeline.
